thread:
camille: quick follow-up from the fragmentation rfc — we saw p99 latency spikes during aggressive slab compaction on mixed workloads. idea: switch to a smoothing approach where we mark candidate free runs and do background coalesce with a rate limit rather than immediate inline compaction. needs a small API boundary between allocator and evictor. thoughts?

ryan: ack. can you sketch the API surface? also worried about cross-tenant fairness if background compaction hogs IO/CPU.

camille: sketch below (pseudo):

```
// allocator.h
void mark_for_compact(PageRunHandle h); // mark free run as compact candidate
size_t compact_batch(size_t max_bytes); // attempt to coalesce up to max_bytes, return freed bytes
```

evictor will call compact_batch from a low-priority worker. compact_batch only merges adjacent free spans, no relocation of live pages.

ajay: question — how do we ensure small-allocation p50 isn't regressed? background compaction must yield to fastpath and avoid touching hot caches. maybe run with cgroup cpuset affinity.

tanya: agree on fairness. suggest per-tenant compaction tokens and a leak-rate so each tenant only uses X bytes/sec for compaction work. also add telemetry hooks: compaction_attempts, compaction_bytes, compaction_time_ms_hist.

kevin: add metric 'frag_ratio' = (free_runs_weighted / total_pages) and 'avg_free_run_len' so policy can decide when compaction is high ROI vs noop. also track compaction_retries.

camille: good metrics. rollout plan: default conservative policy (compact only when frag_ratio>0.25 and avg_free_run_len<8) and an aggressive Dedicated knob. we'll gate via config flag.

ryan: perf tests to add: mixed-size allocation replay (small heavy + occasional large tensors), measure p50/p99 for alloc/free path and throughput before/after compaction. include synthetic fragmentation generator.

ajay: ABI note — allocator callers expect pointer stability; ensure mark_for_compact is only for free runs and does not relocate live allocations. if we want relocations later, that's a bigger RFC (needs quiesce and move semantics).

camille: yep — clarify in RFC update: no move of live pages, only coalesce free spans. if relocation is needed later we'll introduce relocate API and safety checks.

build-bot: CI: Perf/regressions job queued for branch frag-smooth-1768009001 — https://ci.internal/jobs/1768009001 :robot_face:

camille: next steps: I'll draft RFC addendum with API prototypes, metrics, and experiment plan. tagging @ryan @ajay for early review. thanks! :+1:

ryan: quick nit — ensure compact_batch runs on low-prio threadpool and has a retry backoff when compaction yields < threshold bytes freed. also add trace events: compact_start/compact_end with tenant id.

tanya: add that trace and also an event when we skip compaction due to token exhaustion, so we can tune leak rate.

camille: noted — will include trace events and skip reasons in the RFC. aiming to get a prototype in a branch next week.

ajay: lgtm, please include a smoke test that asserts no pointer moves and validates free-run counts before/after.

camille: will do. thanks all.
